RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

As stated in Diary 3 one of the two apprentices who were injured, namely, Tong Yoong Jing(湯永菁), was still detained in the Lester Chinese Hospital. At 1.20 p.m. on the 8-12-38 a telephone message was received at Louza Station from the Lester Hospital to the effect that this man had died at 1.30 p.m.
8-12-38.

Doctor's certificate reads:-
"This is to certify that Tong Yoong Jing(湯永菁) died at 12.40 p.m. 8-12-38 from Septicemia due to general sepsis resulting from multiple bomb wounds over abdomen, face, larynx extremities and chest".

The body of the deceased has been removed to the Public Mortuary pending inquest. The manager of the bookstore and the deceased's family have been informed and representatives will attend the inquest.

In view of the fact that this man has died as a result of the injuries he received when the bomb exploded it is respectfully suggested that the case should now be re-classified as Murder instead of Intimidation.

November 10, 1938.
Morning Translation

Ta Mei Jian Feo and other local newspapers :-

AFFAIRS OF THE WORLD BOOK COMPANY

The main factory of the World Book Company
(世界書局) is located on Dalny Road, Since
its occupation by the Japanese military, the Japanese
authorities have on several occasions detailed officials
to enter into negotiations with the company in the hope
of securing its co-operation under the bait of returning
its property. The offer was, however, rejected by the
company because its property in Hongkew had already been
leased to the American Enterprise Company (美國企業公司).
This refusal on the part of the World Book Company incurred
the displeasure of the Japanese authorities and in revenge
a hand grenade was placed in the business office of the
company the other day. The matter is at present under
careful investigation by the Settlement Police.
Sometime last month, 1,700 cases containing
about 3,000,000 books were removed by the Japanese
authorities from the Hongkew plant and transported to
Japan by a Japanese transport. While the books were
being removed, many of them were seized and detained by
the Settlement authorities who are at present making
enquiries into the actual facts of this case. On
November 8 and 9 another batch of books to the number
of about 1,000,000 packed in 2,000 sacks were removed
to the transport "Myoken Maru" which left here at 9 a.m.
yesterday. It is said that the removal of these books
was undertaken by the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha. According
to the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, they undertook the removal
on instructions from the Japanese military authorities;
they stated that the sacks contained military supplies.
Upon learning of the removal, the American Enterprise
Company at once opened negotiations with the Japanese
authorities but failed to obtain any result.
It is learned that most of the books removed
are medical treatises.

世界书局事务

世界书局（World Book Company）的主要工厂位于大连路。自被日军占领以来，日本当局曾多次派遣官员与公司进行谈判，企图以归还财产为诱饵，换取公司的合作。然而，该公司拒绝了这一提议，因为其在虹口的财产已出租给美国企业公司（American Enterprise Company）。世界书局的这一拒绝招致了日本当局的不满，作为报复，日前一枚手榴弹被放置在该公司的营业办公室内。此事目前正由租界警方仔细调查中。
上月某时，日本当局从虹口工厂移走了装有约三百万册图书的1,700箱货物，并由一艘日本运输船运往日本。在搬运书籍期间，其中许多被租界当局扣押并扣留，当局目前正在调查此案的实际事实。11月8日和9日，另一批约一百万册装在2,000个麻袋中的书籍被搬上运输船“妙见丸”（Myoken Maru），该船于昨天上午9时离开此地。据悉，这些书籍的搬运工作由三井物产株式会社（Mitsui Bussan Kaisha）承担。据三井物产株式会社称，他们是奉日本军方当局的指示进行搬运的；他们声称麻袋内装的是军需品。得知搬运消息后，美国企业公司立即与日本当局展开谈判，但未获任何结果。
获悉被移走的图书大多为医学论著。

CHINA PRESS.
NOV 3 1938

Two Hurt As
Bomb Explodes
In Book Store

Firm Denies Reports
Linking Them With
Puppet Regime

Tang Yung-chin, salesman, one of the two members of his calling injured in yesterday's bombing of the World Book Company, Ltd., 390 Foochow Road, probably will recover from his wounds but it will be several weeks before he returns to work.

The other wounded salesman is Chu Lung-teh. The latter is not seriously hurt, but hospitalization, at least for the time being, has been necessary. Both men are in the Lester Chinese Hospital.

The bombing occurred about 10.20 a.m. yesterday when a time-bomb found on the premises by one of the salesmen suddenly exploded. Property damage was slight.

Rumors Denied

Reports appearing in the Japanese press yesterday are believed to have been responsible for the bombing, according to information made available to both the police and the local press last night.

These reports stated that the World Book Company, Ltd., and the Chung Hwa Book Company, another big Chinese publishing house, are planning to co-operate with the "Reformed Government" to start a joint publishing company.

In a statement issued last night, officials of the World Book Company flatly denied these reports. "No one in this company is connected with these rumors," continued the statement.

The officials added that they have never been approached regarding the question of a merger with the Chung Hwa Company and that the Japanese Press reports were based on the stuff of which dreams are made.

Mysterious Package

The bomb responsible for the blast was found by a salesman, Chu Lung-teh, on a counter in the sales office of the company's store yesterday morning. The time of its discovery was 10.15 o'clock. The infernal machine was wrapped in newspapers and is believed to have been left on the premises by someone who had slipped into the building from the street.

Believing that some customer had walked off, forgetting a purchase, Chu was about to remove the wrapping to investigate the contents when the bomb inside exploded. Strangely enough, he was only slightly injured about the hands. Tang Yung-chin, another salesman, who was standing only a few feet away, was seriously hurt and his recovery is expected to take several weeks.

Detectives of the Louza Police Station, who are engaged in the investigation of the case, are inclined to believe that the terrorists responsible simply walked into the sales office yesterday morning or the day previous, posed as customers and left the bomb on the counter.

Firm Founded In 1911

The World Book Company, Ltd., founded in 1911, is one of the three largest publishing houses in China. The printing plant is located at 130 Dahny Road, while its sales department is maintained at the Foochow Road address. It also has 40 branch houses in various parts of the country.

Mr. C. C. Woo is the present acting chairman of the board of directors, while Mr. K. I. Loh is the general manager. The sales manager is Mr. K. K. Liu. Before the beginning of hostilities in Shanghai, the company's employees numbered about 1,000 persons. Due to the fact that the war made it necessary to close down the printing plant, only 100 workers are now on the payroll.

Since the withdrawal of the Chinese from this area, the plant has been occupied by the Japanese military. The place was damaged during the fighting, according to company reports, while last June, three Chinese and one Japanese were arrested by the S.M.P. for allegedly stealing stocks of books from the premises.

Early last July, it is stated, the Dahny Road plant was leased to the Associated American Industries, Inc., 235 Hamilton House. The American concern is reported to have repeatedly asked the Japanese to hand over the premises but without success.

《字林西报》。
1938年11月3日

书店炸弹爆炸
两人受伤

公司否认有关其与傀儡政权勾结的报道

唐永金（Tang Yung-chin，音译），售货员，是昨日福州路390号世界书局有限公司（World Book Company, Ltd.）爆炸案中受伤的两名同行之一，他可能会从伤势中康复，但需数周后才能重返工作岗位。

另一名受伤的售货员是朱隆德（Chu Lung-teh，音译）。后者伤势不重，但至少暂时需要住院治疗。两人均在莱斯特华人医院。

爆炸发生在昨天上午10点20分左右，当时一名售货员在现场发现的一枚定时炸弹突然爆炸。财产损失轻微。

否认谣言

据昨晚向警方和当地媒体提供的消息，昨日日本报纸上出现的报道被认为是导致此次爆炸的原因。

这些报道声称，世界书局有限公司和中华书局（Chung Hwa Book Company，另一家大型中国出版机构）正计划与“维新政府”合作，成立一家联合出版公司。

在昨晚发表的一份声明中，世界书局的高管断然否认了这些报道。声明继续说道：“本公司无人卷入这些谣言。”

高管们补充说，他们从未就与中华书局合并一事接触过，日本报纸的报道纯属无稽之谈。

神秘包裹

造成爆炸的炸弹是昨天上午由公司门店销售办公室的一名售货员朱隆德在柜台上发现的。发现时间为10点15分。这枚地狱机器/炸弹用报纸包裹着，据信是由某个从街上溜进大楼的人留在现场的。

朱某以为是有顾客离开时忘记拿走购买的商品，正准备拆开包装查看内容物时，里面的炸弹爆炸了。奇怪的是，他仅手部受轻伤。站在仅几英尺外的另一名售货员唐永金受了重伤，预计需要数周时间才能康复。

负责调查此案的老闸捕房侦探倾向于认为，肇事的恐怖分子只是在昨天上午或前一天走进销售办公室，假扮成顾客，将炸弹留在柜台上。

公司成立于1911年

世界书局有限公司成立于1911年，是中国三大出版机构之一。印刷厂位于大连路130号，销售部则设在福州路地址。它在全国各地还有40家分店。

吴先生（C. C. Woo，音译）是现任代理董事长，罗先生（K. I. Loh，音译）是总经理。销售经理是刘先生（K. K. Liu，音译）。在上海战事开始前，公司员工人数约为1,000人。由于战争导致印刷厂不得不停产，目前领薪水的工人仅有100人。

自从中国人撤离该地区后，该工厂已被日军占领。据公司报告，该地在战斗中受损，去年6月，三名中国人和一名日本人因涉嫌从现场偷窃库存书籍而被上海公共租界工部局警务处逮捕。

据说，去年7月初，大连路工厂已出租给位于汉密尔顿大厦235号的联合美国工业公司（Associated American Industries, Inc.）。据报道，这家美国公司曾多次要求日本人移交该场所，但未成功。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

NOV 3 1938

Bomb Kills Man,
Injures Another
World Book Co. Premises
In Foochow Road Scene
Of Outrage

A young Chinese shop assistant was fatally injured and another wounded less seriously yesterday morning when a bomb contained in a parcel exploded at the World Book Co., Ltd., 290 Foochow Road. The parcel had been left at the shop three days previously by a Chinese who made a small purchase. As the man did not call for it, two assistants proceeded to open it at 10.10 o'clock, with the result that the contents exploded while in the hands of one of them.

He suffered such serious injuries that he died a few hours afterwards in the Lester Hospital. The other injured man was peppered with fragments of the bomb in the face, chest and hands. He is expected to recover fully.

The bomb was fashioned from books the inside of which had been hollowed out.

Chief Inspector A. H. Chamberlain, Detective-Inspector G. Bennett and other police from Louza Station hurried to the scene as soon as the alarm had been sounded and questioned several witnesses concerning the man who had left the death-dealing parcel.

Last night the management of the Company issued a statement saying that their printing plant in Yangtszepoo had been occupied by Japanese military since last year and that it was still so occupied despite the fact that it had been leased, last July, to the Associated American Industries, Incorporated, a firm with offices in Hamilton House.

The management further stated that no warning preceded the placing of the bomb on October 30.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，

1938年11月3日

炸弹炸死一人，
致另一人受伤
福州路世界书局 premises
成为暴行现场

昨日上午，一枚藏在包裹内的炸弹在福州路290号世界书局有限公司（World Book Co., Ltd.）爆炸，致使一名年轻华籍店员受致命伤，另一人伤势较轻。该包裹是三天前由一名购买了少量商品的华人留在店内的。由于此人未回来取走包裹，两名店员于10点10分着手打开包裹，结果其中一人在手持包裹时，内物发生爆炸。

他伤势极重，数小时后在莱斯特医院（Lester Hospital）身亡。另一名伤者面部、胸部和手部被炸弹碎片击中。预计他将完全康复。

该炸弹是用内部被挖空的书籍制成的。

总督察A. H. Chamberlain、侦探督察G. Bennett及其他老闸捕房（Louza Station）的警员在警报响起后立即赶赴现场，并就留下该致命包裹的男子情况询问了数名证人。

昨晚，该公司管理层发表声明称，其位于杨树浦的印刷厂自去年以来一直被日军占领，尽管去年7月已将其租给设在汉密尔顿大厦（Hamilton House）的美商联合工业公司（Associated American Industries, Incorporated），但至今仍被占领。

管理层进一步表示，在10月30日放置炸弹之前，并未收到任何警告。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

NOV 2 1938

Grenade Wounds
Book Salesmen
In Foochow Rd.

Time-Bomb Explosion
Lands Two Chinese
In Hospital

BOMBERS MAKE
GOOD ESCAPE

Owners Think Mistake
Made; Print Plant
Held By Japanese

Two salesmen at the World Book Company, 390 Foochow Road were wounded when a time-bomb, placed on the counter by unidentified persons, exploded at 10.20 this morning. Both were rushed to the Lester Hospital where one of them, Tang Yung-chin, was reported in a serious condition. Property damage was not heavy.

Ranked as the third largest publishing house in China, the World Book Company publishes many kinds of textbooks for Chinese schools. The head sales office is located on Foochow Road, near Fokien Road, while its printing factory is on Dalny Road, in the Wayside district.

Parcel Found

One of the salesman, Chu Lung-teh, this morning discovered a parcel, wrapped in newspapers, on the counter. While making inquiries about the owner, the bomb inside the wrapping exploded. Mr. Chu was only slightly wounded but his colleague, Tang, who was standing a few yards from him, sustained serious wounds.

The circumstances under which the bomb was placed on the counter are unknown. It was believed, however, that the terrorists had walked into the sales office posing as customers and left the bomb behind. Police of the Louisa Station are investigating.

Motives Unknown

Exact motives for the terrorist act remain unknown. Officials of the company hinted, however, that the bombing was the result of a misunderstanding. The printing factory of the World Book Company, they pointed out had been under Japanese occupation. It was understood that the Japanese were operating the factory to print Japanese edited textbooks for Chinese schools in the occupied areas. This might have led to a misbelief that the company was cooperating with the Japanese and eventually to the "anti-traitor" bombing, it was believed.

Since July, almost a year after the Japanese occupation of the Dalny Road plant, the officials revealed, an American firm, to whom the factory had been rented, has been making futile attempts to take over the premises from the Japanese. Two months ago, they also recalled, a large quantity of books, stolen from the Dalny Road premises, was found being carted through Foochow Road. Police were called and the property detained. As the company filed claims for the return of the stolen books, the Japanese authorities also are said to have requested their return to the Dalny Road godown. The issue was finally referred to the First Special District Court, where a decision is still pending.

Officials of the company emphatically denied rumors that they were operating the factory for the Japanese and declared that the bombing this morning was a complete surprise, as no warning or threatening notes have been received in advance.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》（SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY）。

1938年11月2日

手榴弹炸伤
福州路书商

定时炸弹爆炸
致两名华人
入院

投弹者
成功逃脱

业主认为系误会；
印刷厂被日军占据

今晨10点20分，不明身份者在福州路390号世界书公司（World Book Company）柜台放置的一枚定时炸弹爆炸，炸伤两名售货员。两人均被急送莱斯特医院（Lester Hospital），据悉其中一人汤永琴（Tang Yung-chin）情况危急。财产损失不重。

世界书公司被列为中国第三大出版机构，为中国学校出版各类教科书。其总销售处位于福州路近福建路处，而其印刷厂则位于越界筑路区的大连路（Dalny Road）。

发现包裹

今晨，售货员之一朱隆德（Chu Lung-teh）在柜台上发现一个用报纸包裹的包裹。在查询物主时，包装内的炸弹爆炸。朱先生仅受轻伤，但站在几码外的同事汤先生受了重伤。

炸弹被放置在柜台上的具体情况尚不清楚。然而，据信恐怖分子伪装成顾客走进销售处，留下了炸弹。老闸捕房（Louisa Station）警方正在调查。

动机不明

此次恐怖行动的确切动机仍不清楚。然而，公司官员暗示，轰炸是由于误解造成的。他们指出，世界书公司的印刷厂一直处于日军占领之下。据了解，日军运营该工厂，为占领区的中国学校印刷经日本编辑的教科书。据信，这可能导致人们误以为该公司与日本人合作，并最终导致此次“反汉奸”轰炸。

公司官员透露，自今年7月以来，即在大连路工厂被日军占领近一年后，一家承租该工厂的美国公司一直试图从日本人手中收回该处所，但徒劳无功。他们还回忆说，两个月前，大量从大连路处所被盗的书籍被发现正通过福州路用车运送。警方接到通知后扣留了这批财产。由于该公司提出了归还被盗书籍的索赔要求，据说日本当局也要求将书籍归还至大连路仓库。此事最终提交至第一特区法院，目前判决尚未下达。

公司官员坚决否认有关他们为日本人运营工厂的谣言，并声明今晨的轰炸完全出乎意料，因为此前未收到任何警告或威胁信件。

November 3, 1938.                                      Morning Translation

Chinese American Daily News :-

THE BOMB EXPLOSION AT THE WORLD BOOK CO.

        The World Book Co. (世界書局) is one of the
leading publishing companies in Shanghai. Its main plant
is on Delny Road, Hongkew, with a general sales office at
No.390 Foochow Road. Following the outbreak of Sino-
Japanese hostilities on August 13 last year, its plant in
Hongkew was occupied by the Japanese army.
        At 10.10 a.m. yesterday an explosion took place
at the sales office and two employees named Tong Yung-jing
(湯永琴) and Tsu Loong-teh (朱隆德) were wounded. The
Police were informed and the wounded men were removed to
hospital.
        According to a statement made by a senior
employee of the bookstore, yesterday morning a paper
parcel was noticed lying on the counter and nobody came
forward to claim it. Tong Yung-jing, an employee of the
store, took up the parcel and finding it quite heavy, he
started to open it to ascertain the contents. On removing
the paper wrapper, he found an iron box made in the form
of a book. Out of curiosity, he attempted to force it
open with some instrument when suddenly it exploded,
wounding him in the face and neck, while another employee
named Tsu Loong-teh who was standing near him was also
injured.
        As the bookstore had not received any warnings,
the cause of the affair is unknown. It is said that the
main plant of the bookstore in Hongkew, which has been
occupied by the Japanese, is being operated by a number
of unscrupulous elements, working under the instructions
of the Japanese. The Japanese have on several occasions
sent men to persuade the bookstore (? for what purpose
not stated), but this was turned down by the bookstore
for the plant was leased to the American Enterprise
Company (美國企業公司) in July this year. Books to the
value of $800,000 were stored at the Hongkew plant, but
most of them had been burned by the Japanese soldiers,
while a quantity was removed with the permission of a
certain party. On one occasion officers of the Settlement
Police seized a truckload of these books. They are still
lying at Central Police Station. At the time of the
seizure a certain party attempted to recover them by force
but was prevented by the Police. In August or September
this year the Japanese requested the bookstore to detail
representatives to the New Asia Hotel (新亞酒店) to
discuss certain arrangements, with the return of the
stock of books as a bait, but the invitation was ignored.
Since then the bookstore had no further trouble. It is
believed that a certain party may be responsible for the
explosion.
        It is also said that the Japanese have recently
organized a "Central China Printing Company" (華中印刷公司)
with the World Book Co. as one of the promoters. The
Hongkew plant of the bookstore was re-named the No.1
printing plant of the "Central China Printing Company".

《中美日报》:-

世界书局炸弹爆炸案

        世界书局是上海主要的出版公司之一。其主要工厂位于虹口大连路，总销售处位于福州路390号。继去年8月13日中日敌对行动爆发后，其在虹口的工厂被日军占领。
        昨日上午10点10分，销售处发生爆炸，两名名为汤永琴（Tong Yung-jing）和朱隆德（Tsu Loong-teh）的雇员受伤。警方接到通知，伤者被送往医院。
        据书店一名高级雇员陈述，昨日上午注意到柜台上放着一个纸包，无人前来认领。书店雇员汤永琴拿起包裹，发现相当沉重，便开始打开以查明内容物。除去纸包装后，他发现一个做成书形的铁盒。出于好奇，他试图用某种工具强行打开，突然发生爆炸，炸伤了他的面部和颈部，而站在他附近的另一名雇员朱隆德也受了伤。
        由于书店未收到任何警告，事件原因不明。据说，书店位于虹口的主要工厂被日军占领后，正由一些在日本人指示下工作的不法之徒运营。日本人曾多次派人劝说书店（？目的未说明），但被书店拒绝，因为工厂已于今年7月租给美国企业公司（American Enterprise Company）。价值80万美元的书籍储存在虹口工厂，但大部分被日本士兵烧毁，另有一部分经某方许可被移走。有一次，租界警察官员扣押了一卡车这些书籍。它们至今仍存放在中央捕房。在扣押时，某方试图武力夺回，但被警方阻止。今年8月或9月，日本人要求书店派代表到新亚酒店（New Asia Hotel）讨论某些安排，并以归还库存书籍为诱饵，但该邀请被无视。此后书店未再遇到麻烦。据信，某方可能对爆炸负责。
        另有说法称，日本人最近组织了一家“华中印刷公司”（Central China Printing Company），世界书局是其发起者之一。书店位于虹口的工厂被更名为“华中印刷公司”第一印刷厂。

All this might have created some misunder-
standing among the patriotic elements who then delivered
the warning. The bookstore, however, has strongly refuted
the report that it has any interest in the bogus
organization.

The "Globe" reports that the rumours prevalent
are all untrue. It appears that the bomb was secretly
planted by a traitor. The Police are examining the
fragments of the bomb recovered at the scene of the affair.

Notice Issued By The World Book Company

The World Book Company publishes the following
notice in the advertisement columns of the "Chinese-American
Daily News" and other local newspapers to-day :-
"About 10 a.m. November 2 certain dangerous
articles placed previously by some unknown person in the
Sales Department of our firm exploded, wounding two employees.
We thank all the schools, bookstores, cultural bodies and
other circles, which had either called or sent telephone
messages of consolation.
"Since the outbreak of hostilities in
Shanghai, our firm has sustained tremendous losses. The
general factory in Hongkew, which had been leased to the
American Enterprise Company, has not yet been recovered
despite repeated negotiations. It is a matter for deep
regret that we should now have been attacked in this way.
We shall continue to devote ourselves to culture and carry
on our business as usual."

《环球报》（The "Globe"）报道称，流传的谣言均不属实。看来炸弹是由一名汉奸秘密安置的。警方正在检查在事发现场回收的炸弹碎片。

世界书局发布的通告

世界书公司今日在《中美日报》及其他本地报纸的广告栏刊登以下通告：-
“11月2日上午10时许，先前由不明身份者放置在我司销售部的某些危险物品发生爆炸，致两名雇员受伤。我们要感谢所有致电或打电话表示慰问的学校、书店、文化团体及其他各界人士。
“自上海战事爆发以来，我司遭受巨大损失。位于虹口的总工厂已租给美国企业公司，尽管经过多次谈判，尚未收回。令人深感遗憾的是，我们现在竟遭到此类攻击。我们将继续致力于文化事业，照常营业。”

At 10.10 a.m. November 2nd, a bomb exploded in
the World Bookstore, 390 Foochow Road injuring two shop
assistants one of whom subsequently succumbed to his
injuries. The infernal machine was concealed in a parcel
of books which had been left on a counter of the shop on
October 31st by an unknown Chinese customer. While
endeavouring to pry open the contents of the parcel, the
bomb exploded in the hands of the deceased assistant.
Assistance was rendered to Louza Station by
Special Branch and Mr. Loh Kao I (陸高誼), General
Manager of the World Bookstore was thoroughly questioned
by D.S.I. MacAdie and D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien with a view
to discovering a motive for the attack. Mr. Loh
expressed the opinion that it was probably connected in
some way with the matter of the Dalny Road printing plant
of the firm. The works at 130 Dalny Road is at present
being operated by the Japanese Special Service Section
with a number of former employees of the firm. It is
at present engaged in printing text books for the schools
under the jurisdiction of the Reformed Government.
On July 1st however the property was leased to the
Associated American Industries Inc., 235 Hamilton House
of which Mr. W. P. Wilson is the Manager. This Company
incorporated in the State of Delaware is stated to be
registered at the American Consulate-General and has made
several unsuccessful attempts to possess the Dalny Road
plant. Regarding the stock of books at the plant,

My name is Loh Kao I, aged 39, native of Shaoshing,
residing at 153 Route Pere Robert. I am the General Manager
of the World Bookstore, 390 Foochow Road which was founded
in 1911 and has about 40 branch houses throughout the country.
Before the hostilities, about 1,000 men were employed at the
printing plant of the firm at 130 Dalny Road and at the

only. The plant has been occupied by the Japanese Military
since the hostilities and is at present being operated by the
Japanese Special Service Section with a number of ex-employees
of the firm who are working entirely without the approval of

我叫陆高谊，39岁，籍贯绍兴，居住于罗别根路153号。我是福州路390号世界书局的总经理，该局成立于1911年，在全国约有40家分店。战事爆发前，公司在大连路130号的印刷厂及书店共雇佣约1000人，但现在仅书店雇佣约100人。自战事爆发以来，该工厂一直被日军占领，目前由日本特务机关运营，雇有该公司的一些前雇员，这些人的工作完全未经管理层批准。

今年6月，中央捕房逮捕了三名中国人和一名日本人，罪名是盗窃从大连路工厂拿走的一批书籍。该案仍在审理中，此后中央捕房的小林副督察曾数次要求管理层直接与日本当局接触以达成和解，但管理层予以拒绝，只同意通过工部局警务处进行处理。

然而，6月份，公司董事同意将大连路工厂以及位于chemulpo路（注：原文如此，疑为Chemulpo即仁川路，或指某特定路名）和朗格路（Rangoon Road，今余姚路）转角处的一处未开发工厂（亦为我方财产）出租给美方利益集团。

通过 N.F. Allman 先生的努力，成立了美商联合工业公司，并于7月1日接管了这两处物业的租赁权。这家美国公司

The case is still pending and the management has since been,

My name is To Loong Tuh age 23, native of Pinghu,

At 2.30 p.m. 31-10-38, a male Chinese (described

However, the man failed to return for the parcel so

the parcel in order to ascertain the contents.

The contents proved to be what appeared to be five
or six thin books stuck together and I was unable to separate
them with my fingers.

November 1, 1938.

MAINLAND

ESTABLISHMENT OF THE HWACHUNG PRINTING CO.

A plan to establish a printing
company to be known as the "Hwachung Printing Co."
which will control all printing business in the area under
the jurisdiction of the "Reformed Government" has been
considered by Mr. Kawai of the Tokaido Book Shop, who is
the chairman of the Committee for the proposed company.

On October 24 the following matters
were formally decided upon:-

The capital of the Company will be Yen 5,000,000
of which Yen 1,000,000 will be subscribed for by the
"Reformed Government" in the form of the property belonging
to the World Book Company, the Chunghwa Book Company and
the Yung Hwa Printing Company in Shanghai and the balance
of Yen 4,000,000 will be taken up by Japanese.

The inauguration of the Hwachung
Printing Company will take place at Shanghai about the
beginning of next month.

June 16, 38.
"Censorship of school textbooks" - further information regarding
the source of this manifesto.

Information was conveyed to D.S.I. Mac Adie by Mr.
Saunders-Bates, editor of the Morning Leader, to the effect
that the local Chinese bookstores were actually responsible
for the issue of the manifesto opposing the order of the
Reformed Government for the examination of textbooks.
In the last sentence of paragraph 2 of the manifesto,
the X X Bookshop mentioned is said to be none other than
the World Book Store, with offices at 390 Foochow Road and
large factory premises at No.130 Dalny Road. The factory
is at present occupied by Japanese military. The premises
are undamaged but the state of the machinery is not known.
The World Bookstore is definitely known to be printing
school textbooks in accordance with the wishes of the Dah
Dao City Government and most probably in return the management
have been promised protection and the eventual return of their
factory property in the Yulin Road area.

J.L.... Kobayashi visited Room 224-226, 89 Foochow
Road and assisted the undersigned in further enquiries.
From enquiries made by J..... Kobayashi it had been
ascertained that the Japanese Military had sold the books
for $3.00 per picul, because it was considered that
some of the books were of anti-Japanese nature and the
same were destroyed. After the books had been seized
Mr. Yuki had been instructed to dispose of the same and
the latter approached a man named Zukichi Suzuki to
carry out the said instructions. Z.Suzuki asked Aikio
Kobayashi to sell the books and the latter removed the
same to his office "Dah Zung Inland Navigation and
Transportation Coy with the assistance of his employee
named Tomijiro Osato. T.Osato obtained the required
pass from the Japanese Military Police and about 4 days
ago, he started to remove the books to 89 Foochow Road
in Mr. Kobayashi's m/car.
As this case involved Japanese Military Authorities,
J.D.S.Kobayashi telephoned to the Japanese Military
Police and Corporal Hasegawa visited the address in
question and promised to render the required assistance,
in clearing up the case.
The Japanese Military Police refused to hand over
the books found at Rooms 224-226, 89 Foochow Road to

小林（J.L.... Kobayashi）访问了福州路89号224-226室，并协助签署人进行进一步调查。经小林（J..... Kobayashi）调查查明，日本军方以每担3.00美元的价格出售了这些书籍，因为认为部分书籍具有反日性质，这些书籍已被销毁。书籍被查获后，雪先生受命处理这些书籍，随后他联系了一位名叫铃木善吉（Zukichi Suzuki，音译）的人来执行上述指示。铃木善吉请求小林爱雄（Aikio Kobayashi，音译）出售这些书籍，后者在其雇员佐藤富次郎的协助下，将书籍搬至其办公室“大达内河航运运输公司”（Dah Zung Inland Navigation and Transportation Coy，音译）。佐藤富次郎从日本宪兵队获得了所需的通行证，并于大约4天前开始使用小林先生的机动车将书籍搬运至福州路89号。
由于本案涉及日本军方当局，日本副领事小林（J.D.S. Kobayashi）致电日本宪兵队，长谷川下士（Corporal Hasegawa）访问了上述地址，并承诺提供必要协助以澄清此案。
日本宪兵队拒绝将福州路89号224-226室发现的书籍移交给

the International Settlement Police but promised that
they will keep the books at the same place until the
case is carefully investigated. Two Chinese who had
been detained by the Police as stated above, were
removed to the Central Police Station and together with
a man named Fee Keng eng, they had been detained by
the Police for further enquiries.
They will appear before the .. .. ..Court on July
14th when application will be made for their detention
for one week on a Writ of Detention pending further
enquiries.
Sang Pau Ling, chauffeur, was released and allowed
to drive M/car Lic.No.10317 to his employer's house.
I.O."A" and I.I.O."A" had been informed regarding
this case.

国际租界警方，但承诺在案件得到仔细调查之前，将书籍保留在原处。如上所述，被警方拘留的两名华人被移送至中央巡捕房，并与一名叫费根生（Fee Keng eng，音译）的人一起，被警方拘留以作进一步讯问。
他们将于7月14日出庭于.. .. ..法院，届时将申请依据拘留令将他们拘留一周，以待进一步讯问。
司机桑宝林（Sang Pau Ling，音译）获释，并被允许驾驶牌照号为10317的机动车返回其雇主家中。
“A”区情报官（I.O."A"）和“A”区内部情报官（I.I.O."A"）已获悉此案情况。
